questions.q: Which of the following is a polar aprotic solvent?
questions.explain: DMF, H–CO–N(CH₃)₂, is polar but has no H on O or N, so it cannot donate hydrogen bonds. Acetic acid, methanol and formic acid all carry an O–H and are protic.

questions.q: The correct order of nucleophilicity of halide ions in DMSO is:
questions.explain: In a polar aprotic solvent the anions are bare, so nucleophilicity follows basicity and F⁻ is best. The order I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻ applies in protic solvents, where small F⁻ is hydrogen-bonded most strongly.

questions.q: The reaction of 1-bromobutane with azide ion is fastest in:
questions.explain: SN2 of an anion is speeded up by polar aprotic solvents, which leave the nucleophile unsolvated; acetonitrile gives a relative rate of 5,000 against 1 in methanol. Hexane cannot even dissolve the azide salt.

questions.q: According to the Hughes–Ingold rule, increasing solvent polarity will:
options: Speed up both the SN1 solvolysis of tert-butyl chloride and the SN2 reaction of OH⁻ with CH₃Br
Have no effect on either, since both involve the same leaving group
Slow down the SN1 solvolysis of tert-butyl chloride but speed up the SN2 reaction of OH⁻ with CH₃Br
Speed up the SN1 solvolysis of tert-butyl chloride but slow down the SN2 reaction of OH⁻ with CH₃Br
questions.explain: Charge is created in the SN1 transition state of a neutral substrate, so a more polar solvent speeds it up; in SN2 of an anion with a neutral alkyl halide the charge is spread out, so higher polarity slows it down.
